A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TRACED with the same authors, framework, and benchmarks. All 31 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison despite substantial reordering.

before.justification: V1 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments on MiniGrid and BipedalWalker, including zero-shot results, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and training trajectories.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds worker-count experiments and quantitative curriculum-progression analysis.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 revises the stated replay weights from proportional to TaskPriority to proportional to its reciprocal; v3 explicitly assigns rank 1 to the highest difficulty-plus-Co-Learnability score. This is a limited revision of the documented sampling rule. The combined loss, Co-Learnability calculation, networks, and mutation loop remain unchanged; an implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 12 MiniGrid evaluation tasks, PerfectMazeLarge and PerfectMazeXL, and six BipedalWalker terrains. The added worker-count experiment changes configuration within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The main-text ablation comparison in Figure 10 drops standalone ACCEL, retaining full TRACED and its two single-component ablations. ACCEL remains in the corresponding appendix table. The benchmark comparators remain DR, PLR-perp, ADD, ACCEL, and the same indirectly estimated ACCEL-CENIE results.

E3.justification: Appendix A.4 adds a 32-worker MiniGrid comparison at 5k and 10k updates. Section 4.4 introduces explicit terrain-parameter thresholds for classifying BipedalWalker curriculum difficulty. Figure 10 now reports aggregate ablation metrics. The primary 16-worker MiniGrid and four-worker BipedalWalker settings were already documented in v1.

E4.justification: V3 adds a focused worker-count robustness check and quantifies Easy, Moderate, and Challenging curriculum proportions over training. Existing component and weight ablations, terrain visualizations, and 45k-update oscillation analyses are retained; the long-term analysis is relocated rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: V1 Table 9 specifies five-seed MiniGrid ablations, including subsampling five of ten TRACED and ACCEL runs. V3's discussion of the unchanged Table 12 instead says ten seeds, while Section 4.3 still says five and the subsampling disclosure disappears. V3 also removes the five-seed reference-column qualification from the sensitivity analysis. These are reporting changes, not evidence of additional runs.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark, component-ablation, and sensitivity-table values remain unchanged. New Table 7 reports 32-worker MiniGrid mean solved rates of 0.72 for TRACED versus 0.54 for ACCEL at 10k updates. New Table 2 reports 14.6% Challenging BipedalWalker levels for TRACED versus 0% for ACCEL at 10k. These are added results, not same-setting performance improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Equation 2 replaces the Q*-minus-Q, two-error decomposition with a V*-minus-Q-policy expression involving value-estimation error, reward gap, and future-value gap. V1's Co-Learnability proposition and expected-staleness theorem, including both Appendix A proofs, are removed entirely. This substantially revises the paper's formal foundation.

C1.justification: V3 removes the explicit up-to-twofold environment-interaction claim from the abstract and the numerical PerfectMaze and BipedalWalker improvement claims from the introduction. The two-component contribution, zero-shot generalization claims, and conclusion's half-training-update claim remain.

C2.justification: V3 describes Co-Learnability as a computational surrogate for marginal contribution, adds noisy ATPL under stochastic transitions as a limitation, and qualifies the explanation of long-run oscillations while using them to justify reporting at 10k updates. The separate random-mutation/CMA-ES limitation is removed. Most applicability boundaries remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 newly describes an ACCEL-matched warm-up and clarifies how its worker counts and network choices relate to inherited settings. The actual hyperparameter values, architecture specifications, software versions, hardware, and code-access information remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds Hughes et al. (2024) on open-endedness and removes Hansen's CMA-ES reference with the mutation-limitations paragraph. It also adds a rationale for excluding SFL, citing already-present Rutherford et al. The broader related-work discussion and positioning against ACCEL and CENIE remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The introduction, method workflow, experimental discussion, and captions receive extensive rewriting. Appendices are substantially reorganized, with long-term analysis moved forward and numerical results moved to the end. Section naming, citation style, and a new LLM-language-editing disclosure further change the document's presentation.

P2.justification: Figure 10 changes from a per-task radar chart to four aggregate interval plots, and two tables are added. Extensive figure/table relocation and resizing accompany the new document style; the long-term plots are consolidated onto one page. Most underlying figure artwork and existing table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added worker-count control and quantitative curriculum analysis strengthen empirical support, while the stochastic-transition limitation improves qualification. V3 also withdraws the staleness guarantee whose v1 proof uses an inequality opposite to its non-increasing-priority assumption. These gains support a modest net improvement, tempered by newly inconsistent MiniGrid ablation seed counts and lost subsampling details. The retained benchmark results are unchanged.
